 ## ref-sorting
 concepts: sorting-key, intervals
 Sort by a tuple key to break ties deterministically: `sorted(c, key=lambda x: (-c[x], x))`.
+
+## ref-search
+concepts: binary-search, two-pointer, monotonic, bisect, search-space
+`bisect.bisect_left(a, x)` is the leftmost insertion point. For a predicate that flips once,
+binary-search the answer: `lo, hi = 0, n` then `while lo < hi:` with `mid = (lo + hi) // 2`.
+Two pointers on a sorted array: advance `l` when the sum is too small, retreat `r` when too big.
+
+## ref-traversal
+concepts: recursion, graph, tree, bfs, dfs, grid, visited
+BFS with `collections.deque` gives shortest hop count; DFS with an explicit stack avoids
+recursion limits. Always mark `visited` at push time, not at pop time, or nodes are enqueued
+twice. Grid neighbours: `for dr, dc in ((1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1))` with an in-bounds guard.
+
+## ref-accumulate
+concepts: dynamic-programming, prefix-sum, memoize, running-state, subarray
+Prefix sums make any range sum O(1): `p[i+1] = p[i] + a[i]`, then `sum(a[i:j]) == p[j] - p[i]`.
+For overlapping subproblems use `functools.lru_cache(None)` on a pure recursive function, or
+carry a single rolling variable when the recurrence only looks back one step.
+
+## ref-edges
+concepts: edge-case, empty-input, off-by-one, boundary, single-element
+Before returning, check the degenerate inputs: empty sequence, one element, all-equal elements,
+and the value at both ends of the range. Half-open ranges `[lo, hi)` compose without off-by-one;
+mixing them with inclusive bounds is the usual source of a one-short or one-long answer.
